clue.text: Admit objective is a bad mistake

parts.note: to own up is to admit, so to own means to admit
a goal is an objective or aim

explanation.surface: Confessing that your aim was a serious blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: An own goal, in football, is a score put into your own net, hence any self-inflicted blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: A self-defeating blunder is called this, from football where a player scores against their own side.

clue.text: Line up on vessel for religious service

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top, reversed

parts.note: a row is a line of things
a ship is a sea vessel

explanation.surface: Queuing to board a ship for a church service.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns ROW into WOR; 'on' places it above SHIP in the down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Worship is a gathering for prayer and praise of God, a religious service.

clue.text: Not the best man to take care of horses

definitions.meaning: at a wedding the bridegroom stands beside the best man but is not him
to brush and tend horses, as a stable hand does

explanation.definitionFit: The man getting married at a wedding, and the verb for brushing and tending horses.

clue.text: Makes a legal charge

parts.note: read plainly, brings a charge against someone; 'charge' might also suggest a fee or a cavalry attack

explanation.definitionFit: To accuse someone is formally to charge them with an offence or wrongdoing.

clue.text: Add 51 to 49 — a hundred? It is wrong!

parts.note: in Roman numerals 49 is written IL (one before fifty), a loose crossword convention
in Roman numerals 51 is LI, fifty plus one
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
taken as written

explanation.surface: A muddled sum adding numbers up to a hundred, declared incorrect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Add ... to' only strings the numerals together: 49 first, then 51, then C and IT. Strictly 49 is XLIX in Roman numerals; IL is a setter's licence.
explanation.definitionFit: Something illicit is unlawful or forbidden, which is a sense of wrong.

clue.text: Pulse is fast — over one fifty

parts.note: Lent is the Christian season of fasting
I is the Roman numeral for one
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A racing heartbeat runs past one hundred and fifty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pulse' and 'fast' suggest a heartbeat; a pulse is also an edible seed such as a pea or bean. 'over' places LENT above I and L in the down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Lentils are pulses, the dried edible seeds of leguminous plants.

clue.text: Sick jokes producing bad feeling?

parts.note: ill means sick
humour, the stuff of jokes

explanation.surface: Tasteless jokes cause resentment.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill humour is a sour, irritable mood, a state of bad temper.

clue.text: Fit, full of energy for the time being

indicators.note: full of means the energy letter sits inside the word for fit

parts.note: in trim means fit, in good condition
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Feeling fit and energetic at the moment.
explanation.definitionFit: Interim describes something provisional, lasting only until a permanent arrangement, for the time being.

clue.text: Practise how to be a pickpocket

definitions.meaning: to regain skill by doing something repeatedly
taken literally, a pickpocket puts a hand into a victim's pocket

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to practise to regain a skill; literally, slipping one's hand into a pocket, as a pickpocket does.

clue.text: Group of musicians — or it could be

indicators.note: says the letters of 'or it' could become something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: A band, or perhaps something else entirely.
explanation.definitionFit: A trio is a set of three performers playing together, one kind of musical group.

clue.text: Char works overtime to wipe off debts

parts.note: a char is a cleaning woman, so what a char does is clean: she cleans
working late is working overtime

explanation.surface: A cleaning lady puts in extra hours to clear what she owes.
explanation.walkthrough: A char (British) is a woman paid to clean houses. The definition is loose: a fresh start with debts wiped off.
explanation.definitionFit: Starting with a record cleared of past debts or faults is starting with this.

clue.text: Eats with the best

definitions.meaning: to champ is to chew noisily
short for champions, the winners who are top

explanation.definitionFit: Champs is both a verb for munching food and slang for champions, those judged finest.

clue.text: Late item for the press

parts.note: sounds like breaking news arriving at deadline, but 'late' means dead: a newspaper piece about someone who has died

explanation.surface: A last-minute story rushed to the newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: A notice of a person's death, with a short account of their life, printed in a newspaper.

clue.text: Work on chair, say, with higher armrest

parts.note: up means higher, as in prices going up
read as arm-rest: a holster is where a firearm rests

explanation.surface: Fixing a chair by raising its armrest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Armrest' looks like part of the chair; split it as arm (a gun) plus rest, a gun's resting place.
explanation.definitionFit: To pad and cover furniture such as a chair with fabric; 'say' marks a chair as one example.

clue.text: Exaggerated account discredited

definitions.meaning: an ... picture is exaggerated, drawn beyond the truth
a bank account with more taken out than is in it, in debit

explanation.definitionFit: Overdrawn means overstated or exaggerated, and describes a bank account in debit.

clue.text: Follow scholar's teachings

parts.note: to dog someone is to follow them closely
MA, Master of Arts, a degree held by a scholar

explanation.surface: Adopting a learned person's lessons as a disciple.
explanation.definitionFit: Dogma is the body of doctrine laid down by an authority, a set of teachings.

clue.text: Religious retreat for sailor and Turk

parts.note: AB, able seaman, a sailor
a bey is a Turkish governor or title, so a Turk

explanation.surface: A sailor and a Turk both seek refuge in a monastery.
explanation.definitionFit: An abbey is a monastery or convent, where monks or nuns withdraw from the world.

clue.text: Square the difference

definitions.meaning: to square accounts is to make them ...
the amount remaining, the difference between credit and debit

explanation.definitionFit: Balance as a verb means to square accounts; as a noun the remainder or difference between two sums.

clue.text: Two wines favoured in York

parts.note: white is one kind of wine
rosé is another kind of wine

explanation.surface: A pair of wines popular in a northern English city.
explanation.walkthrough: The white rose is the emblem of Yorkshire and the House of York, worn in the Wars of the Roses.
explanation.definitionFit: This flower is York's chosen emblem, the badge the Yorkist side adopted.

clue.text: Crying, having finally got a reprimand

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word got

parts.note: an earful is a scolding, a reprimand

explanation.surface: In tears after at last being told off.
explanation.definitionFit: Tearful means weeping or close to tears, crying.

clue.text: Cross sailor gets over anger

parts.note: an old salt is a sailor
ire is anger

explanation.surface: An angry sailor gets over his temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like angry, matching the surface; it is the noun: a saltire is a diagonal X-shaped cross, as on Scotland's flag. 'gets over' places SALT above IRE.
explanation.definitionFit: A saltire is an X-shaped heraldic cross, St Andrew's cross on the Scottish flag.

clue.text: He arranges the grave stone to be assembled about ten

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go around the ten symbol
the stone letters are to be assembled in a new order

parts.note: X is the Roman numeral for ten

explanation.surface: A gravestone is put together at around ten o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be assembled' makes SETON from STONE, and 'about' puts X inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A sexton is a church officer whose duties traditionally include digging graves.

clue.text: Leg bound to be broken by heavy stick

indicators.note: the leg and bound letters are to be broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: A bound leg is fractured by a blow from a club.
explanation.definitionFit: A bludgeon is a short thick club used as a weapon.

clue.text: Moon rocket gets ahead on oxygen

parts.note: split as a head: A plus POLL, an old word for the head
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: A space rocket moves forward using oxygen fuel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ahead' looks like forward motion; split it as 'a head', A + POLL (poll is the head, as in poll tax).
explanation.definitionFit: The NASA programme that landed astronauts on the Moon flew rockets and craft under this name.

clue.text: Ring an agent up at Covent Garden?

parts.note: O is ring-shaped

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means reading the words an agent from bottom to top

parts.note: a rep, representative, is an agent

explanation.surface: Telephoning a representative at a London theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns A REP into PERA. Covent Garden is home to London's Royal Opera House, so the name stands for opera; the question mark flags this.
explanation.definitionFit: Covent Garden in London houses the Royal Opera House, so the name is shorthand for the art form staged there.

clue.text: One who steals gets frantic if he's taken

indicators.note: frantic suggests wild disorder, so the letters of if he's taken are jumbled

explanation.surface: A thief panics at the thought of being caught.
explanation.definitionFit: A sneak thief pilfers quietly without breaking in, a stealthy kind of robber.

clue.text: Correct reversal of flow

indicators.note: says the word for flow is to be read backwards

parts.note: the tide is the flow of the sea

explanation.surface: Putting right a change in direction of a current.
explanation.definitionFit: To edit text is to correct and revise it.

clue.text: Incorrect in angle?

indicators.note: incorrect says the letters are wrongly placed and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: Asking whether something is set at the wrong angle.
explanation.walkthrough: As a whole the clue describes the answer: something tilted is out of true, wrong in its angle.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tilting is set off the vertical, so its angle is not true.

clue.text: Delighted when record return took the pressure off

indicators.note: return says the record's letters come back in reverse

parts.note: LP, a long-playing record
eased means relieved, took the strain off

explanation.surface: Relief at a record being returned brings joy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when' is a link; 'return' turns LP into PL.
explanation.definitionFit: To be pleased is to feel glad or happy, a mild form of delighted.
